article.intro: In Greek myth, the sirens sang from their island so beautifully that sailors steered onto the rocks to reach them. Odysseus had himself tied to the mast to hear them and live. This **siren name generator** makes Greek-sounding names, song-names like Wavecall, and sirens named for the shore they haunt.

sections.heading: The sirens of Greek myth
sections.content:
In Homer's Odyssey, the sirens sing from their island so sweetly that sailors steer onto the rocks to hear them.

  • Odysseus had his crew block their ears with beeswax and tie him to the mast, so he could hear the song and live.
  • Jason's Argonauts got past them another way: Orpheus played his lyre louder than they could sing.
  • Bird-women: in Greek art sirens have the bodies of birds and the heads of women. They only became fish-tailed sea-maidens in the Middle Ages, which is why siren and mermaid are now mixed up.
  • Names: Homer doesn't name them, but later writers give names like Parthenope, Ligeia and Leucosia. Parthenope's body was said to have washed ashore where Naples now stands.

sections.heading: Naming a siren
sections.content:
• Greek names use the old sea and song words (Thelxiope, "charming voice"), with a home "of the Black Rocks".
  • Song names describe the voice that does the damage: Foamsong, Stormhymn, Drownsigh.
  • An epithet says what the song does to you.

faqs.question: How did Odysseus survive the sirens?
faqs.answer: He had his crew plug their ears with beeswax and tie him to the mast, so he could hear the song without steering onto the rocks.

faqs.question: Were sirens mermaids?
faqs.answer: Not originally. In ancient Greek art they were part woman and part bird. The fish-tailed siren came later, in the Middle Ages.

faqs.question: What are the sirens called?
faqs.answer: Homer doesn't say. Later Greek writers name them, with names like Parthenope, Ligeia and Leucosia.
